newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Wednesday at $63.00 per cwt were passed by owners seeking $65.00 to $66.00, feedlot sources said.
Several feedlot operators said they expect fed cattle to trade steady to up $1.00, compared with last week's active sales at $64.00.
"I think it's going to happen today, but just don't know at what level, its going to be an interesting day," one Texas Panhandle feedlot manager said.
Prices were expected to be supported by continued strong beef prices and current feedlot marketings, they said.
Boxed beef prices Tuesday were quoted down $0.02 per cwt to up $1.15 per cwt, with the heavier-weight choice up $0.63 at $96.24, USDA said.
This week's showlists were seen unchanged to smaller than last week, which should help keep prices underpinned, sources said.

Cattle demand has been strong, with many of the cattle sold last week already shipped and slaughtered. The quick shipments fueled ideas that packers would be back in the market Wednesday or Thursday, some cattle feeders said.
